subject: Escalation: Zenora strategic partnership — exclusivity & MFN request
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@zenora.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@zenora.ai>; Zenora Legal <legal@zenora.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strategic partnership proposal — exclusivity + MFN

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed. Zenora is moving quickly and we'd like to discuss a short-term strategic partnership tied to product integration and preferred pricing. High level asks: 

- 12-month regional exclusivity for major retail customers in North America (with carve-outs for existing integrations)
- A Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) clause on list pricing for the first 18 months
- Performance benchmark tied to latency/p99 that would trigger price adjustments

We attached a draft SOW for context. We see this as a pilot that could scale enterprise-wide. Can your team review and let us know what internal approvals are required?

Daniel
Director of Partnerships
Zenora AI
Attachment: Zenora_SOW_v1.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Strategic partnership proposal — exclusivity + MFN

Team — forwarding Zenora's ask. Key points: 12-month NA exclusivity, MFN for 18 months, benchmark-linked pricing. They frame it as a pilot but want preferred pricing and exclusivity in major retail accounts.

Quick take: I think MFN + region exclusivity are high risk for product and GTM. Need legal's redline and revenue view. Karthik, please add expected ARR and probability if we accept. Neha, can you run a quick risk assessment and flag non-starters? Connor, any commercial levers (time boxes, caps, carve-outs) you recommend?

I want to consolidate a recommended position and escalate to Markus for final sign-off by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Irene
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Strategic partnership proposal — exclusivity + MFN

I reviewed the draft SOW and did an initial risk pass. Summary here and attached: internal_risk_note_exclusivity.pdf (short memo).

Top concerns:
- Regional exclusivity is asymmetric: it limits future go-to-market with other strategic partners and complicates marketplace listings.
- MFN for 18 months is broad — it can force us to retrospectively match a lower price and compress our pricing motion across deals.
- Benchmark-triggered price adjustments are ambiguous; the SOW lacks defined measurement, tolerance and dispute resolution.

Suggested guardrails if we proceed:
1) Convert 'exclusivity' to a limited, customer-segmented pilot: 90 days, limited to a named pilot account list (max 3 accounts), and opt-out on mutual agreement.
2) MFN: limit to incremental discounts only (not list price) and cap exposure (e.g., max 20% rebate cap) with liability limits and audit rights.
3) Benchmarks: define telemetry, sample size, and an independent verification clause; price adjustments should be prospective only.

I'll attach a tracked-redline to the SOW. On legal risk scale (1-10) I'd put this at 7 unless we narrow the exclusivity and MFN scopes.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Zenora_redline_track_changes.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Strategic partnership proposal — exclusivity + MFN

I ran quick revenue math on the table Zenora shared. If we accept full MFN + broad exclusivity, upside ARR looks like $2.4M in year 1 with a 75% probability — but that assumes they commit to a minimum consumption floor which they haven't. Risk is that MFN forces price compression across future renewals.

Recommended commercial compromise (preferred path):
- Time-box exclusivity: 6 months, limited to a named pilot list (max 5 customers) with a clear termination/extension mechanism.
- MFN: limited to the specific SKU/feature set in the SOW, and only applies to new customers introduced by Zenora; cap total exposure to $200k in rebates over 18 months.
- Benchmarks: change to SLA credits (capped) rather than automatic price reduction; allow 30-day validation window and arbitration clause for disputes.

If Markus signs off on these guardrails, Neha can present a redline we can take back to Daniel. Without those, I recommend declining exclusivity and offering a strategic priority lane (short-term co-marketing + integration commitment) instead.

Karthik
VP, Strategic Sales
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Executive approval request — Zenora partnership (summary + recommended position)

Markus,

Summary: Zenora is asking for NA exclusivity (12 months), an 18-month MFN clause, and benchmark-linked pricing. Legal flags this as high risk (score 7/10) primarily due to the scope of exclusivity and the breadth of the MFN. Revenue expects meaningful upside only if they commit to a minimum spend; current draft lacks that.

Recommendation (we request your sign-off):
1) Approve pursuing a pilot under the following guardrails: 6-month time-boxed, named-account exclusivity (max 5 customers), opt-out clause.
2) Approve a limited MFN that applies only to incremental discounts on the specific SKUs in the SOW, with a $200k rebate cap and audit rights.
3) Change benchmark clauses to SLA-credit style remedies (prospective) with independent verification and a 30-day remediation window.

If you approve, we'll send Neha's redline and Karthik's commercial language back to Zenora. If you decline, we'll propose an integration + priority support alternative without exclusivity or MFN.

Requesting a decision by EOD today (9 Apr) so we can keep momentum.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: internal_risk_note_exclusivity.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive approval request — Zenora partnership (summary + recommended position)

Irene — thanks for the concise summary and recommendations. I agree with the conservative path. Approve proceeding with the pilot under the guardrails you outlined (6 months, named-account exclusivity, MFN limited to incremental discounts with $200k cap, SLA-credit remedy).

Two asks before you send the redline back: 1) include a clause that automatically converts any extended exclusivity to a commercial review with Finance and Product; 2) ensure we have an explicit minimum consumption commitment from Zenora before exclusivity takes effect.

Markus
COO, Redwood Inference
